newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-ITALIANS WEIGH UP MERITS OF OXFORD 'EDUCATION'.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ITALIANS WEIGH UP MERITS OF OXFORD 'EDUCATION'.

text.p: The prospect of Italy's future soccer stars completing their football education in a city more famous for welcoming scholars than strikers was shrouded in uncertainty on Wednesday.

English first division side Oxford United caused a stir by revealing plans to set up an exchange programme with Juventus, which would involve the Turin club's most promising youngsters being loaned out to experience how the British play the game.
Juventus officials have visited the homely Manor Ground -- capacity 9,572 -- for discussions, but chairman Robin Herd's visions of a unlikely relationship have yet to be approved by the Italians.

"We've got a chairman who's got a lot of contacts in the Formula One world and that is where the link comes from," said general manager Ian Davies, referring to the Agnelli family's connections in both Juventus and Ferrari.
"We didn't particularly want it to come out now. It's still at the 'talks about having talks' stage.
"We hope something does come of it and a lot of people are asking what we're planning. But it's dangerous to fall in love with an idea. It's a question of watch this space."
A Juventus spokesman said on Wednesday he was unable to comment.
Oxford currently lie in 11th place in the first division, 22 points behind leaders Bolton.
